title: Customer Feedback Analysis with a Business Taxonomy and Budgeted Review Selection: An Offline Evaluation
content: Small and medium-sized enterprises need feedback analyses that identify actionable issues under limited review budgets. We link a declared business taxonomy, multi-label classification, budgeted review queues, and convention-weighted issue priorities. SemEval-2016 laptop annotations are mapped deterministically to seven analytical labels, and no new human labels are claimed. On 808 held-out laptop fragments, lexicon-augmented logistic regression reaches macro F1 0.4778 against 0.4572 for plain logistic regression, yet the plain model has fewer joint state errors (672 versus 687) and lower priority mean absolute error (MAE: 0.01344 versus 0.01768). At a 10% budget the validated joint queue finds 109 of 687 state errors against 100 for uncertainty and 68.56 for random selection. Perfect replacement of selected fragments lowers error counts but raises priority MAE for the impact-only queue, because contributions are signed. Claims are limited to the 808 held-out fragments: offline queue discovery compares predictions with supplied gold states, ideal correction assumes perfect replacement, and neither measures observed reviewer effectiveness.
